sre-alex: Alert — p99 latency SLO burned in euw1 for hosted-infer. Spike started ~15:12 UTC, accompanying 5xx/timeouts. Opening thread to correlate customer reports and observability.
oncall-bot: [ALERT] hosted-infer.euw1.p99_latency > 1200ms (SLO burn) — firing: see runbook /incidents/hosted-infer-slo
support-jordan: Seeing a few customer escalations: ticket #2345 (Notea) and #2348 reporting 502/504s in the 15:10–15:30 window. They sent sample request ids but some are missing traces.
observability-eli: Grafana panel shows a clear spike in gateway 504s at 15:11–15:16. Trace sampling dropped dramatically at the same time (~70% trace gap). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/hosted-infer/euw1-latency
eng-lina: Can someone paste the log query you used? I'll start slicing by backend host and request path.
observability-eli: Quick query I used (Loki):
```
{job="hosted-infer-gateway", region="euw1"} |= "UpstreamTimeout" | json | line_format "${status} ${request_id} ${upstream_host}"
| count_over_time(1m)
```
Filter shows concentrated timeouts towards upstream pool `infer-pool-7`.
sre-alex: Noted. Support reports align with that pool. Hypothesis: a transient downstream slowdown (batcher or model worker) causing gateway timeouts + trace drop. Immediate mitigations: 1) enable model fallback to smaller variant, 2) expand dedicated pool by +2 nodes for euw1, 3) temporarily raise request timeout to 30s for canary customer routes.
oncall-bot: Autoscaler attempted add: requested 2 nodes to infer-pool-7 at 15:18 UTC — provisioning in progress. Current pool size +0 -> +1 pending (cloud quota check passed).
